subject: Post-call: performance acceptance criteria & customer-led load test plan
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Patel <rajiv@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-30T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: perf SLOs & customer-led load test next steps

Hi Rajiv / Priya,

Thanks again for the call today — good alignment on goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the customer-led load runbook scheduled: 

Key acceptance criteria you confirmed on the call:
- 95th percentile tail latency <= 220ms for conversational generation (streaming enabled, avg token length ~15)
- Sustained throughput target: 1200 requests/minute with bursts to 1800 rpm for up to 10 minutes
- Concurrency target: 60 concurrent user streams with an expected average of 8 ongoing tokens per stream
- Successful streaming reconnect behavior within 2s for transient interruptions

Action items I captured: 
1) Acme to provide the final k6/Locust test script or a short sample traffic profile (we can adapt) — due by Fri 2027-05-07
2) Redwood to provision a test account + API key and send IP allowlist template — I'll attach the template and a starter k6 script now
3) Agree on a 3-hour customer-led test window (preferred: Tue 2027-05-11 09:00-12:00 PDT) and an alternate (Thu 2027-05-13 16:00-19:00 PDT)
4) Capture SLO measurement points (we'll instrument request/response times, server-side processing, and stream latency) — see attached SLO matrix for proposed metrics and alert thresholds

Attachments: acme_k6_script_v1.js (starter), acme_allowlist_template.csv, slo_matrix_acme.xlsx

If that looks right, can you confirm the preferred test window and whether you’ll supply the k6 script or want us to run the supplied starter script?

Thanks — I’ll loop in Rishi for runtime tuning if you want quantization/throughput tradeoff guidance.

—
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
From: Rajiv Patel <rajiv@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: perf SLOs & customer-led load test next steps

Hi Hannah — thanks for the clear summary. Confirming a few items from our side: 

- The SLOs look good. We may relax the 95th to 240ms if we see significant degradation on long contexts, but let's target 220ms as the acceptance bar.
- We'll supply our Locust-based scenario (it simulates speech-to-text + generation fan-out) by COB 2027-05-06. Can you confirm any required dependency versions or helper endpoints your starter script expects?
- We prefer Tue 2027-05-11 09:00-12:00 PDT for the test window. If we need more than 3 hours we'll flag it, but aim to fit the primary run there.

A couple of questions: 
1) For streaming reconnects — will Redwood's SDK surface an event we can assert on, or should our test harness track socket-level reconnects?
2) Do you need our source IP ranges in CIDR form? We'll provide both the CIDRs and a short list of hostnames.

We'll attach the Locust scenario to the thread tomorrow. Thanks — excited to get this running.

Best,
Rajiv
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Analytics
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap: perf SLOs & customer-led load test next steps

Hannah / Rishi — forwarding Rajiv's confirmation. Heads up on a couple of preflight checks we'll want to run before the customer window: 
- Sanity-check the k6/Locust script on a non-prod sandbox (we can run a 30-minute dry run to validate error rates and token distribution)
- Ensure the API key we'll issue is scoped to a throttle/bucket that mirrors production for a fair test, but isolated so we don't impact other customers
- Rishi: if you can pre-populate the KV cache with a sample prefix set (they mentioned some hot prompts), that will reduce cold-start noise during the primary ramp. 

I'll take lead on sandbox runs and test account provisioning. Rishi, please advise on expected memory/cpu footprints for the 60-concurrency scenario so we can confirm capacity.

-Marissa
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T08:29:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call recap: perf SLOs & customer-led load test next steps

Thanks — quick datapoints: based on similar workloads, for 60 concurrent streaming sessions with average token churn of ~8 per stream we expect:
- GPU memory: ~22–28 GB reserved (depends on quantization); recommend a 40GB headroom on the dedicated instance during the window
- CPU: 8–12 vCPUs for coordinating proxy/service mesh and streaming glue
- Network: allow for bursty egress; measure up to 150 Mbps sustained during peak bursts

I'll prepare a short runbook snippet for max-resources vs cost-optimized modes (we can toggle quantization levels and batching targets). Also will pre-warm KV cache as requested — please confirm the sample prefixes they plan to use.

-Rishi
From: Rajiv Patel <rajiv@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya@acmeanalytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T11:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: perf SLOs & customer-led load test next steps

All good — confirming the Tue window 2027-05-11 09:00-12:00 PDT. We'll attach the Locust scenario and a CSV with our source CIDRs and hostnames by EOD 2027-05-04.

Answers: 
- We'll track socket-level reconnects in the harness but would love any SDK events you expose; if there is an event hook we can subscribe to that would make our assertions cleaner.
- CIDRs will be in the attached allowlist CSV (format per your template).

Thanks for the runbook notes Rishi — we can share the set of hot prefixes for pre-warm today. Please go ahead and provision the test API key and send connection details.

Attachments in next email: acme_locust_scenario_v1.py, acme_source_cidrs.csv

Regards,
Rajiv
Director, Platform Engineering, Acme Analytics
